title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook - Overview and Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response standards: incident lifecycle, runbook templates, postmortem process, on-call rotations and handoffs, game day guidance, and status page / customer communications templates. It is intended for SREs, service owners, on-call engineers, and responders.

Scope

- Applies to all production services (Redwood API, routing, inference runtime, Dedicated control plane, telemetry/observability pipelines).
- Operational owners must keep runbooks and playbooks referenced here up to date when making changes to service topology, SLOs, or tooling.

1) Incident classification and severity

We use four severity levels for consistent prioritization and customer communication:

- Sev 1 (P0): Major outage or degradation impacting >25% of customers or causing severe data loss or safety issues. Target response: 0-5 minutes; full mitigation target: 1 hour.
- Sev 2 (P1): Large functional degradation impacting a significant subset of customers, degraded SLOs, or heavy performance regressions. Target response: 5-15 minutes; mitigation: 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (P2): Partial degradation affecting a narrow set of customers or non-critical functionality. Response: within 30 minutes; mitigation: 24-72 hours.
- Sev 4 (P3): Non-urgent issues, maintenance, or known issues with scheduled fix. Response during business hours; remediation per regular backlog processes.

Key SLO examples and alert thresholds

- Redwood API availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Latency targets: p95 < 350ms (small models), p99 < 1s.
- Error rate threshold: API 5xx < 0.1% (0.001).

Alert examples:

- Pager alerts for API 5xx > 0.5% sustained for >3 minutes.
- Region p99 latency > 1.5s for >5 minutes.
- GPU node OOM/eviction: immediate pager.

2) Incident lifecycle (quick checklist)

- Detect: alert triggers or customer report.
- Triage: Primary acknowledges in PagerDuty and begins scope assessment.
- Notify: Create incident in Jira (INF-INCIDENTS) and post initial summary to #incidents.
- Mitigate: Execute runbook play or traffic fallback.
- Restore: Confirm metrics returned to acceptable SLOs.
- Recover: Implement durable fix and open follow-up tickets.
- Postmortem: Publish per severity timelines (see section 5).

3) Roles and escalation matrix

- Primary (Pager): first responder; owns triage and immediate mitigation.
- Secondary: backup for domain knowledge and weekend escalation.
- Engineering Manager (EM): engaged for coordination and prioritization when needed.
- Incident Commander (IC): appointed for Sev1 to run the war room and control cross-team actions.

Standard escalation timings

- Primary acknowledge: within 5 minutes for Sev1, 15 minutes for Sev2.
- Escalate to Secondary if no progress in 10 minutes (Sev1).
- Appoint IC and escalate to EM if no containment in 60 minutes (Sev1).

Communication channels and tools

- PagerDuty: Redwood-API-Pager.
- Slack: #incidents (coordination), #infra-ops (engineering), #cust-comm (customer comms drafts).
- Incident tracking: Jira INF-INCIDENTS.
- External status page: status.redwood.ai.

4) Runbook template (per-service, owned by service team)

Fields to include:
- Title: <service-name> production runbook
- Maintainer: <name and team>
- Last updated: <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Contacts: pager schedules and owner email

Immediate triage steps (ordered):
1. Acknowledge in PagerDuty.
2. Determine scope: affected regions, endpoints, sample errors.
   - Example command: kubectl -n production logs deploy/redwood-api --since=10m | grep "ERROR" | head -n 50
3. Check recent deploys: curl https://ci.redwood.internal/api/latest-run?service=<service-name>
4. Verify infra: kubectl get nodes -o wide; nvidia-smi (via admin jumpbox).
5. Check caches/datastore: Redis INFO, RDS replica lag, slow query logs.
6. Apply mitigation: traffic shift, feature flag rollback, scale replicas, or switch to fallback model.
   - Example traffic swap: curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/route/swap -d '{"from":"v2","to":"v1"}'
7. Observe metrics for at least 15 minutes before closing incident.

Common mitigation plays:
- Rollback a problematic deploy and re-run smoke tests.
- Cordon/drain GPU node and scale up pool.
- Clear per-session KV cache and trigger patch for cache corruption.

Resolution checklist:
- Metrics stable within SLOs for 15+ minutes.
- Short-term mitigation or permanent fix identified.
- Follow-up Jira tickets created with owners and due dates.
- External comms and status page updated where applicable.

5) Postmortem process and template

Timelines:
- Assign postmortem owner within 24 hours for Sev1/Sev2.
- Draft published within 7 calendar days.
- Finalized postmortem with action items triaged within 30 days.

Postmortem template (Confluence):
- Title: [SEV1] short description - <YYYY-MM-DD>
- Summary: one-sentence impact and duration.
- Timeline: detailed, timestamped sequence of events (UTC).
- Impact: affected customers/features/metrics, estimated business impact.
- Root cause analysis: causal chain with supporting logs/metrics.
- Contributing factors: tools/process/human factors.
- Corrective actions: short-term mitigations and long-term fixes with owners/due dates.
- Detection & response analysis: what worked, what failed, and recommendations.
- Links: PRs, Jira tickets, runbooks updated.

Cultural expectations:
- Focus on systems and remediation, not individuals.
- Use data to support conclusions and list evidence for assertions.

6) On-call rotations and handoffs

Rotation policy:
- Primary: weekly rotation (Mon 09:00 UTC -> next Mon 09:00 UTC).
- Secondary: staggered weekly pairing.
- EMs/senior SREs act as backups for holidays.

Handoff checklist (Slack handoff):
- Active incidents and current status.
- Recent deploys and known risks.
- Scheduled maintenance windows.
- PagerDuty escalation changes and contact updates.

Time-off and swaps:
- Declare planned time-off >2 weeks in advance.
- For urgent swaps, follow PagerDuty swap workflow and notify #oncall-ops.

7) Game days and exercises

Purpose: validate runbooks, tooling, and cross-team coordination; reduce MTTR.

Planning steps:
- Objective, scope, participating teams, and failure scenarios.
- Schedule: 1 week planning, 1 day execution, 1 day retrospective.
- Artifacts: inject scripts, dashboards to monitor, and retrospective notes.

Sample scenario (multi-region failover):
1. Simulate eu-west-1 control-plane outage.
2. Initiate routing policy to shift traffic to us-west-2.
3. Measure failover time, p99, and error rate.
4. Run external comms and update status page.
5. Conduct retrospective and update runbooks.

8) Status page and customer comms templates

Status page rules:
- Create incident on status.redwood.ai for public-facing incidents.
- Initial update within 15 minutes for Sev1; hourly updates while active.
- Entries must be factual, non-speculative, and include an ETA for the next update.

Initial external short subject:
- [Identified] <short description> - Impacting API requests in <region>

Initial external message (first post):
- Summary: We are investigating an issue affecting <service> in <region>. Customers may see elevated errors and latency. Our on-call team is working on mitigation.
- Impact: affected endpoints and approximate percent of customers.
- Next update: by <UTC time>.
- Contact: support@redwood.ai for urgent impact.

Follow-up update template:
- What changed since last update: mitigation steps taken.
- Customer guidance: workarounds or retry guidance.
- ETA or timeline for next update.

Final resolution template:
- Summary: Incident resolved. Root cause: <brief RCA>.
- Timeline: start and end (UTC), impact summary.
- Next steps: postmortem link and corrective actions.

Customer email (major incidents)
Subject: Incident summary - <service> degradation on <YYYY-MM-DD>
Body:
Hello <CustomerName>,

We want to inform you about an incident that affected <service>.

Timeline:
- Start: <UTC time>
- Mitigated: <UTC time>
- Resolved: <UTC time>

Impact: <endpoints and affected customers>.
Root cause: <high-level RCA>.
Remediation: <what we did and long-term fix>.

For billing or compliance impact assessments, reply to this message and Customer Success will prioritize.

Regards,
Customer Success & Ops, Redwood Inference

9) Tooling, storage, and runbook hygiene

- Store runbooks and postmortems in Confluence in service folders and link from the service repo README.
- Keep immediate triage steps concise (<2 pages) and link to detailed diagnostics.
- Label runbooks with last-updated and owner metadata.
- Audit runbook coverage quarterly and after each Sev1 incident.

10) Appendix: quick commands and dashboards

- kubectl: kubectl -n production get pods -l service=redwood-api -o wide
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/redwood-infra/service-overview
- PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/service_redirect?service=Redwood-API-Pager
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/new
